title: Hollow Knight
shortDescription: Team Cherry's breathtaking hand-drawn Metroidvania masterwork exploring the melancholic insect ruin of Hallownest.
historicalSignificance: Widely acclaimed as the pinnacle of the modern Metroidvania genre, hand-crafted by an Australian indie trio (Team Cherry) with colossal scale, airtight nail swordplay, soul-recovery risk, and Christopher Larkin's melancholic chamber orchestral score.

editorialContent.overview: Created in Adelaide, South Australia by three-person indie studio Team Cherry (Ari Gibson, William Pellen, and David Kazi) following a 2014 Kickstarter, Hollow Knight was released on PC in February 2017. As a nameless, silent wanderer wielding a worn nail, players descend into Hallownest, a vast, interconnected subterranean kingdom of insects fallen into ruin and gripped by a sickly glowing infection.
editorialContent.gameplay: Precision 2D platforming combines fluid swordplay, downward nail pogo-bouncing off hazards and enemies, and Soul resource management: striking enemies generates Soul, used either to cast powerful spells or focus to slowly heal masks. A modular Charm notch system allows players to customize their build across over 40 distinct combat and mobility badges.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: Built in Unity with thousands of hand-drawn traditional 2D animation frames, multi-plane parallax depth, and Christopher Larkin's evocative chamber music that dynamically responds to location depth and emotional resonance.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Hollow Knight sold over 3 million copies and elevated Team Cherry to legendary indie developer status, sparking an enduring passionate global fandom eagerly anticipating its sequel, Hollow Knight: Silksong.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved natively on PC via Steam and GOG, as well as physical collector's editions across all modern game consoles published by Fangamer.

technicalSpecs.engine: Unity with Team Cherry custom 2D lighting and physics pipeline
technicalSpecs.soundChip: High-fidelity digital audio with Christopher Larkin live strings and piano score
